nodes.author: LauraMiers
nodes.text: Yep. I don’t even think about SS or retirement because I stayed home with kids for the last 16 years since childcare costs more than college. Covid disabled me the year all my kids reached school age, & I intended to rejoin the workforce. I will likely never work or draw SS. If we’re being honest, I’ll be shocked if I even see 50.

nodes.author: CovidiotDeaths
nodes.text: @LauraMiers @KaiMADAOZen Not to be flippant but I'll take that bet. Sometimes it seems that horrible=hopeless, but it's not. You've made it through the worst, and gotten better. You'll improve more, and see 50 and 60, and almost certainly be able to work.

nodes.author: KaizenMayDay
LauraMiers
nodes.text: That helps to hear! I’ve definitely improved since the first 3 years, but I no longer expect a full recovery. I think shifting into acceptance has helped too. I’m very privileged to have family help, & I worry so much for the people who don’t understand what they’re walking into. I truly don’t know how people are going to make it in this environment.

nodes.author: KaizenMayDay
nodes.text:
@LauraMiers I think there’s too much emphasis on “recovery” which isn’t all that helpful when your body has changed. Acceptance  includes a sense of discovery, knowing you’re moving forward as a new but disabled person. 
It’s what I’ve had to say to myself regarding my own health.

nodes.author: LauraMiers
nodes.text: I couldn’t have said it better myself. For the first 3-4 years, we kept hearing “MOST RECOVER!” while like 7% recovered in 3 years. Individuals blame themselves & think they’re just exceptions, everyone else is doing better than they are, & it’s their fault. Once I quit focusing on recovery & accepting this is how I live now, it helped. The guilt, shame, & blame game causes so much harm.

nodes.author: KaizenMayDay
nodes.text: @LauraMiers It truly does, whether we’re talking physical health, emotional health, relational health or even spiritual health. We have to give  ourselves grace to be changed and to allow our definition of ourselves to change. Shame and blame get us nowhere but stuck. No one deserves this.

nodes.author: LauraMiers
nodes.text: When I got Covid in early 2020, in western NY, I was in & out of hospitals speaking to terrified HCWs who had been seeing patients since Oct 2019. A local family friend & her grandson were hospitalized with mystery pneumonia & “Kawasaki” in Nov. 2019. I personally believe the 6 months of “vape deaths” during the summer of 2019 was early COVID. I don’t think we will ever get the truth.
